status.label: Tracked in the Grab and Move Windows-key issue
status.detail: The thread confirms that Keyboard Manager's Win-key shortcuts fail when Grab and Move uses Win, matching the existing open tracking issue #47585.

judgment.rationale: The report and follow-ups tie inconsistent Win-key shortcut remapping to Grab and Move's Windows modifier. The author and another commenter report that disabling Grab and Move restores the shortcut; another user reports the same behavior on 0.101.2373, and the author confirmed the issue on 0.100.2 with Grab and Move set to Win. Open issue #47585 tracks Grab and Move consuming or interfering with Windows-key hotkeys in Keyboard Manager and other applications. Keep this Windows+shortcut reproduction with #47585 rather than opening a parallel fix path.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.99.1 and maps Win+A to Win+N; the shortcut only partially works or never opens the Calendar pane.
The author and another commenter say disabling Grab and Move restores the shortcut; toggling Grab and Move off and on temporarily restored it.
A later user reports Win+O shortcuts failing on v0.101.2373 while Grab and Move is enabled and working after it is disabled.
The author confirms on v0.100.2 that Grab and Move is enabled with the Windows key and the issue can be reset by toggling Grab and Move.
Open issue #47585 tracks Win-key hotkeys being affected when Grab and Move uses the Windows key, including Keyboard Manager remaps and other applications.
The current issue has nine comments, no assignees, and remains open.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the Win+A/Win+N reproduction with #47585 and avoid a second design for the same Grab and Move modifier conflict.

fix_assessment.rationale: The same Grab and Move / Windows-key hotkey interaction is already tracked in open issue #47585; this report supplies a related shortcut repro rather than an independent fix path.

known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.99.1 and a Win+A-to-Win+N remap.

inferences: The two reports likely share the same Grab and Move / Windows-key hook interaction; no distinct root cause is established.
issue_context.analysis: The current thread establishes a component interaction and points directly to #47585, which has a clearer Win-key hotkey reproduction. Preserve the Win+A/Win+N and Calendar-p pane behavior as corroborating evidence there rather than splitting implementation work.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body and all nine comments, including the Grab and Move toggle reports and the 0.101.2373 follow-up.
